nodes.name: A container died
nodes.notes: Opt in per container with the label selfheal=true, so this never touches something you did not mean it to. Catch-up is on: a container that dies while n8n itself is restarting is still handled, which is exactly when it tends to happen.

nodes.name: Capture logs BEFORE restarting
nodes.notes: Taken first, deliberately. Restarting can rotate or discard the very output that explains the crash, so the evidence is collected while it still exists.

nodes.name: How many times has it restarted?
Confirm it stayed up
nodes.notes: Starting is not the same as staying started. If the container has a health check, change the target to 'healthy' for a much stronger guarantee.

nodes.name: Recovered
nodes.notes: Worth a quiet notification rather than a loud one — but do send something. A container silently restarting nightly is a fault you want to know about eventually.

nodes.name: ALERT: restart did not hold
nodes.notes: Replace with Slack, Discord or email. The item already carries container, exitCode, restartCount and logTail — everything needed to triage without opening a terminal.

nodes.name: ALERT: giving up, needs a human
nodes.notes: The restart limit was reached. Escalate loudly and stop restarting: past this point a restart loop only buries the cause and burns CPU.

main.node: How many times has it restarted?
ALERT: giving up, needs a human
